To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a set of instrumental indices of upper limb (accuracy, velocity and smoothiness) can be computed from 3D endpoint trajectories obtained during a robotic exoskeleton-assisted reaching task; (2) these indices have construct validity, as they are able to discriminate stroke subjects from healthy individuals; (3) these indices have concurrent validity, as they correlate with the Wolf Motor Function Test; (4) these indices are able to discriminate among stroke subjects with the same WMF level.
the indices-based UL assessment has construct validity and can be used to support clinical evaluation of stroke patients’ UL function.
the proposed index-based UL evaluation can be used as a complementary tool to support clinical evaluation in stroke patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of a set of indices that can be used in the clinical practice of UL function assessment.
the validation of a new set of indices to assess UL functionality during robot-assisted tasks.
the use of a robotic exoskeleton for the assessment of UL function in patients with a stroke.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study provides a validation of the proposed instrumental indices, which can be used to assess UL functionality, and that the ArmeoSpring is a valid device to be used for this purpose.
the proposed indices-based UL assessment can represent a valid and reliable alternative to the traditional WMFT assessment.
the proposed indices can be used to assess accuracy, velocity and movement smoothness, and can support clinical UL assessment of stroke patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed indices can be used to assess the residual UL function in stroke subjects.
this assessment is a useful tool to evaluate UL function, and that it can be used to detect differences in UL function among stroke patients.
a set of 4 indices can be used to quantify the accuracy, velocity and movement smoothness of stroke subjects’ UL movements during reaching tasks with an exoskeleton robot.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Armeo-Spring device can be used as a clinical instrument for UL assessment in stroke patients.
the proposed indices can be used to assess the UL function of stroke patients, even when the WMFT is not able to discriminate between different patients’ abilities.
the proposed indices are able to detect differences of residual UL function in stroke subjects, thus representing a valid tool to be used for UL assessment.
